dish: House-brewed beer and fine dining 43 feet underground in the lager-aging Catacombs
address: 102 N Market St, Mount Joy, PA 17552
w: Alois Bube's 1876 brewery in Mount Joy — on the National Register and believed to be the only intact 19th-century lager-era brewery in the US; eat in the stone aging cellars, the biergarten or the Victorian hotel bar.

dish: Whole-animal-butcher burgers and sandwiches — Lancaster County Magazine readers' favorite burger
address: 300 block of N Queen St, Lancaster, PA 17603
w: Chef Steve and pastry chef Lianne Cabalar's whole-animal butcher shop and lunch counter (2018), breaking down local pasture-raised animals in front of you on North Queen Street.

dish: House beers from a brewery that has made 200-plus styles since 1995, with a full brewpub menu
w: Opened in 1995 in the National Register-listed McGovern tobacco warehouse at Plum and Walnut — the first brewery to operate in Lancaster in some 40 years, in a county that brewed 7% of America's beer in 1810.
